speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with sudden-onset vertigo; to determine the cause, please tell me if you experience any hearing loss, tinnitus, or a sensation of fullness in your ear on the affected side?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of brief, sudden-onset vertigo lasting less than a minute without hearing loss or systemic signs is classic for BPPV. I recommend a Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis.
